q: Which appellation's decree requires a blend of at least 40% Mediterranean varieties and at least 40% Atlantic varieties?
exp: Cabardès sits north-west of Carcassonne exactly where the Atlantic and Mediterranean climates meet, and its rulebook turns that geography into a recipe: at least 40% from Grenache Noir and Syrah together, and at least 40% from Merlot and the two Cabernets together. Cot and Fer are permitted only as accessory varieties and count toward neither minimum. No other French appellation compels such a marriage. Malepère, just to the south, is the mirror image rather than a co-holder of the rule — it leans Atlantic with Merlot as its principal variety.

q: What two additional requirements must a Banyuls meet to be labelled Banyuls Grand Cru?
accept: at least 75 percent grenache noir and 30 months in oak
minimum 75% grenache noir, thirty months of barrel ageing
75 percent grenache noir plus 30 months aged in wood
grenache noir three quarters of the blend and thirty months in cask
ans: A minimum of 75% Grenache Noir, and a minimum of 30 months' ageing in wood
exp: Straight Banyuls needs only 50% Grenache Noir and far less ageing, so 'Grand Cru' here describes a recipe and an élevage, not a delimited superior site — the opposite of what the words mean in Burgundy or Alsace, and a favourite trap. The same terraced schist slopes above Collioure also produce dry red Collioure AOP; the grower decides at harvest which wine to declare.

q: What does 'Viñedo Singular' certify in Rioja?

q: Name the bodega founded at Cenicero in 1970 by Enrique Forner that brought Bordeaux methods (Peynaud, cold fermentation, new French oak, early release) to Rioja Alta.
ans: Marqués de Cáceres (Cenicero, Rioja Alta) — French-influenced modern style; built on purchased grower fruit, not an estate
exp: For classicism instead: La Rioja Alta, CVNE, Muga; for the estate revolution: Contador, Artadi (which left the DOCa).

q: Which bodega's 'Castillo Ygay Gran Reserva Especial' released a 1986 white in the 2010s?
